_about: Prices and payment links for /rain-print. Products: digital (the 12 x 18 in digital file of the art, emailed finished within 1 business day of paying, no proof step; Sig redoes it free if the buyer asks for a change), print12x18 (the print on 13 x 19 paper, untrimmed, unframed, shipped flat between chipboard; the ids keep their old names), framed12x18 (the same in a 13 x 19 black frame with a white mat and a glass front, ready to hang); Sig prints, frames and ships them himself. The page reads this file; change a price here and the page follows. payment_links: paste a Stripe Payment Link (https://buy.stripe.com/...) per product. While a link is null, that button opens the order request form instead. The page adds client_reference_id=<design code> to the link, so each Stripe payment carries the design; open https://agsist.com/rain-print?d=<code> to see it. A gift order's code starts with GIFT- (this year's print: make it after January 1, once the full year is in); ?d= opens it with or without that prefix. A long design (a long place, name, line and labels, past Stripe's 200 characters) goes as its short-link id instead: RPS-<id>, or GIFT-RPS-<id> for a gift; rain-print?d=RPS-<id> opens it too, the same as agsist.com/r?<id>. Gift text (this year's print, ordered now and delivered in January): {year} becomes the current year and {next} the year after, on the page and the printed gift card. Say January, not a date: the print waits on NOAA's December numbers. Christmas cutoffs (print_christmas_cutoff, framed_christmas_cutoff, YYYY-MM-DD) are the last day an order still arrives by Dec 24 under the promise on the page: proof within proof_business_days, the buyer OKs it within approve_business_days, it ships within ship_business_days after that (3 since 2026-10-14, Sig; was 7), and the carrier takes transit_business_days per product (weekends and holidays skipped). Change any of those numbers and set the two cutoffs to what RainPrint.christmasCutoff() gives; the test fails until they agree. From October 1 to the cutoff the print and framed cards say "Order by <date> for Christmas delivery."; after it, through Dec 25, they say new orders ship after Christmas. Next year: move holidays and the cutoffs to that year. This year's gift prints ship in January and show no cutoff. For businesses (the quote form under the prices, 5 to 500 prints; the worker refuses fewer than 5): business_cutoff (YYYY-MM-DD or null): when set, the section says "For Christmas, send your list by <Mon D>." through that date; after it, or while null, nothing about a date. business_note (null or one sentence): shown as written under the section; null shows nothing. business_tiers [{min, print12x18, framed12x18}]: from min prints up, each print costs that many dollars, delivered (shipping included, anywhere in the 50 states), one price per print like the cards above. Each tier runs to the next tier's min less one; the last runs to business_quote_max. The first tier's min should stay 5 (the worker's minimum); a tier priced the same as the cards shows as "one invoice, no discount". business_one_address_off {print12x18, framed12x18}: dollars off each print when the whole order goes to one address. business_quote_max: the most prints the table and the form's quote line price; above it (up to the form's 500) the page says Sig quotes it himself. A digital file on a business order is the digital price above at any quantity, emailed. The page builds its table and the form's quote line from these and the prices above. business_tiers empty or missing: no table, and the quote line says Sig quotes it. Consumer orders (the three cards above) never use these. full_year_from (MM-DD): last year counts as finished from this day of the new year once its December is in. Until NOAA has December in (at most 30 days after Dec 31, then a late day is a gap), and before this day, last year is drawn as the year so far and ordered to be made once the full year is in; the print files on the maker page wait too. "01-01" (the default) means as soon as December is in; "02-01" waits for any late corrections through January. reprint_fee (dollars): the fee to reprint or reframe a print lost or damaged in the mail (same serial number), $15 (Sig, 2026-10-14). The refund FAQ says the amount (visible and its structured data); change it here and the page shows the new number, and change the FAQ text to match.
ships_within: Prints and framed prints ship within 3 business days after you approve the proof, anywhere in the 50 states.
_letter_offer: A code on the letter in every print box (components/rp-insert.js, Sig 2026-10-17). Off while code is empty. To turn it on: make the promotion code in Stripe (the same code, a fixed amount off, the same end date), turn on Allow promotion codes on each payment link, then set code (letters and digits, 3 to 20), dollars_off (whole dollars, more than 0) and expires (YYYY-MM-DD, the last day it works, or empty for no end date). The letter then says: Want one for another year or another farm? Use code <code> for $<dollars_off> off at agsist.com/rain-print. Good through <Month D, YYYY>. A letter made after expires, or with any field it cannot read, prints no line.
_canada: Orders from Canada (components/rain-print.js orderPrices, 2026-10-16). A design whose town or station is Canadian orders the digital file today, at the price and checkout above (no shipping). ships is the one switch for prints and framed prints to Canada: false keeps them off for Canadian designs (the cards say shipping to Canada starts soon). true opens them at print12x18 / framed12x18 below (US dollars, shipping to Canada included; null keeps the US price), through payment_links below (a Stripe Payment Link that collects a Canadian address; null opens the order request form, which emails Sig, and he sends a payment link). ships_within replaces the US shipping line for those designs; transit_business_days feeds the arrival date; print_christmas_cutoff and framed_christmas_cutoff (YYYY-MM-DD or null) give Canada its own Christmas dates, and with null no Christmas date is shown for a Canadian design. Prices, carriers and terms are Sig's call; see the plan in the Rain Print Canada notes.

canada.ships_within: Prints and framed prints ship to Canada within 3 business days after you approve the proof. GST/HST is collected on delivery.

gift_delivery: A {year} print ships in January {next}, once the full year is in. A print or framed print gets a proof first, as with every order.
gift_card_title: Your {year} Rain Print is coming in January
gift_card_note: The finished print shows every day of rain from January 1 to December 31, {year}.
_promote: promote:true (on since 2026-10-13, Sig: Rain Print is launched; ordering is the request form until payment_links are filled) turns on the homepage card (components/rain-print-promo.js, after the daily content: Christmas wording from promote_from through framed_christmas_cutoff, then the gift-card wording through Dec 24, otherwise year-round wording), the "see a year of rain here" lines on related pages, and, between promote_from and promote_until only, one line, "A year of your farm's rain, as a gift. Order framed by <framed_christmas_cutoff>.", linking /rain-print, on /cash-bids (under the bids), only while today in America/Chicago is between promote_from and promote_until inclusive (components/rain-print-promo.js). false hides all of these; the menu and footer links stay either way. briefing_line: null for none, or one sentence; with promote on and in the window it shows once near the end of /daily and of the daily email (scripts/brief_email.py rain_print_line).
briefing_line: A year of your farm's rain, printed and framed for the wall: a Christmas gift for the farmer who has everything. agsist.com/rain-print
